title.en: Use Q and K to predict the direction of a reaction
Apply Le Chatelier's principle to changes in concentration, pressure, temperature and catalyst

say.en: Industry makes millions of tonnes of ammonia by pushing an equilibrium the right way. Today we learn how to predict and control the direction of a reaction. In this lesson: Use Q and K to predict the direction of a reaction.
Relate K to delta G degrees.
Apply Le Chatelier's principle to changes in concentration, pressure, temperature and catalyst.

body.en: The *reaction quotient* Q has the same form as K but uses the concentrations at any moment. If Q < K the reaction goes forward; if Q > K it goes backward; if Q = K it is at equilibrium. K is linked to the standard Gibbs energy change by ΔG° = −RT ln K, so K > 1 means ΔG° is negative.
body.kn: ಕ್ರಿಯಾ ಭಾಗಲಬ್ಧ Q, K ಯಂತೆಯೇ ಇದ್ದರೂ ಯಾವುದೇ ಕ್ಷಣದ ಸಾರತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. Q < K ಆದರೆ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಮುಂದಕ್ಕೆ, Q > K ಆದರೆ ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ. ΔG° = −RT ln K.

points.en: Large K (> 10³): mostly products; small K (< 10⁻³): mostly reactants

narration.en: The reaction quotient Q has the same form as K but uses the concentrations at any moment. If Q < K the reaction goes forward; if Q > K it goes backward; if Q = K it is at equilibrium. K is linked to the standard Gibbs energy change by ΔG° = −RT ln K, so K > 1 means ΔG° is negative.

say.en: The reaction quotient Q has the same form as K but uses the concentrations at any moment. If Q is less than K the reaction goes forward; if Q is greater than K it goes backward; if Q equals K it is at equilibrium. K is linked to the standard Gibbs energy change by delta G degrees equals -RT ln K, so K is greater than 1 means delta G degrees is negative. Q is less than K: forward.
say.kn: ಕ್ರಿಯಾ ಭಾಗಲಬ್ಧ Q, K ಯಂತೆಯೇ ಇದ್ದರೂ ಯಾವುದೇ ಕ್ಷಣದ ಸಾರತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ. Q is less than K ಆದರೆ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ ಮುಂದಕ್ಕೆ, Q is greater than K ಆದರೆ ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ. delta G degrees equals -RT ln K.

say.en: Q is greater than K: backward.
Q equals K: equilibrium.
Large K (> 10 to the power 3): mostly products; small K (< 10 to the power minus 3): mostly reactants.

title.en: Predicting direction and Le Chatelier's principle

say.en: Compare the reaction quotient Q with K. If Q is less than K the reaction moves forward; if Q is more, it moves backward; if equal, it is at equilibrium.
ICE table: one mole each of hydrogen and iodine in one litre, K equals 64. Let x react; then 2x over 1 minus x equals 8, so x is 0.8.
Le Chatelier: a system at equilibrium shifts to reduce any change you make.

Ammonia: 4 gas moles give 2, and the forward reaction is exothermic. High pressure helps, and low temperature helps the yield but slows the rate, so industry uses about 700 kelvin and 200 atmospheres with an iron catalyst.
Predicting direction and Le Chatelier's principle.

narration.en: A ⇌ B is at equilibrium. Add A or B and watch the system use up part of what you added until Q is back to K. Changing the temperature changes K itself: up for an endothermic reaction, down for an exothermic one.
narration.kn: A ⇌ B ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿದೆ. A ಅಥವಾ B ಸೇರಿಸಿ: ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಸೇರಿಸಿದ್ದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಬಳಸಿ Q ಮತ್ತೆ K ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ. ತಾಪ ಬದಲಿಸಿದರೆ K ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: If a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts so as to reduce the effect of the change. Adding a reactant or removing a product shifts it forward. Raising pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles. Raising temperature favours the endothermic direction and changes K. A catalyst does not shift the equilibrium, and adding an inert gas at constant volume has no effect.
body.kn: ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿರುವ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೆ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ, ಆ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯ ಪರಿಣಾಮವನ್ನು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುವ ದಿಕ್ಕಿಗೆ ಅದು ಸರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ತಾಪ ಮಾತ್ರ K ಯನ್ನು ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ವೇಗವರ್ಧಕ ಸಮತೋಲನವನ್ನು ಸರಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

problem.en: For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, Kc = 64. At one moment [HI] = 0.50 M, [H₂] = 0.20 M and [I₂] = 0.20 M. Which way does the reaction go?

steps.en: So more HI must form: the reaction goes forward.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. For H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI, Kc = 64. At one moment [HI] = 0.50 M, [H₂] = 0.20 M and [I₂] = 0.20 M. Which way does the reaction go?

say.en: Let us solve this together. For H 2 plus I 2 is in equilibrium with 2HI, Kc equals 64. At one moment [HI] = 0.50 M, [H 2] = 0.20 M and [I 2] = 0.20 M. Which way does the reaction go?
Qc = [HI] squared/([H 2][I 2]) equals 0.25 divided by 0.04 equals 6.25.
Qc 6.25 is less than Kc 64.
So more HI must form: the reaction goes forward.
So the answer is Forward, towards HI.

problem.en: K for a reaction at 300 K is 10. Find ΔG° (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).

narration.en: Let us solve this together. K for a reaction at 300 K is 10. Find ΔG° (R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).

say.en: Let us solve this together. K for a reaction at 300 kelvin is 10. Find delta G degrees (R equals 8.314 joules mol to the power minus 1 K to the power minus 1).
delta G degrees equals minus 2.303 RT log K.
= minus 2.303 times 8.314 times 300 times log 10 equals minus 2.303 times 8.314 times 300 times 1.
= minus 5744 joules mol to the power minus 1 is approximately minus 5.74 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
So the answer is delta G degrees is approximately minus 5.74 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
